incoming.name: Civilization
incoming.excerpt: Archaeologists have discovered a massive, dredged canal and docking facility at the coastal city of Lothal, India, perhaps the world's oldest sea-faring harbour.

outgoing.name: Arsenic
outgoing.excerpt: Lothali copper is unusually pure, lacking the arsenic typically used by coppersmiths across the rest of the Indus valley.

outgoing.name: Bahrain
outgoing.excerpt: An intensive trade network gave the inhabitants great prosperity—it stretched across the frontiers to Egypt, Bahrain and Sumer.

outgoing.name: Calligraphy
outgoing.excerpt: Lothal has yielded 213 seals, third in importance amongst all Indus sites, considered masterpieces of glyptic art and calligraphy.

outgoing.name: English language
outgoing.excerpt: Lothal ( Gujarātī: લોથલ, IPA: /ˈloːtʰəl/, English: Mound of the dead) was one of the most prominent cities of the ancient Indus valley civilization.

outgoing.name: Jewellery
outgoing.excerpt: Their work in metallurgy, seals, beads and jewellery was the basis of their prosperity.

outgoing.name: Mediterranean Sea
outgoing.excerpt: Cemeteries have been found which indicate that its people were probably of Dravidian, Proto-Australoid or Mediterranean physiques.

outgoing.name: Metallurgy
outgoing.excerpt: The techniques and tools they pioneered for bead-making and in metallurgy have stood the test of time for over 4000 years.

outgoing.name: Pakistan
outgoing.excerpt: When India was partitioned in 1947, most of the sites, including Mohenjodaro and Harappa, came to be located in the state of Pakistan.

outgoing.name: Pottery
outgoing.excerpt: A new technique of firing pottery under partly-oxidising and reducing conditions was improved by them—designated black-and-red ware, to the micaceous Red Ware.
